scope: Original OOS decision-time support for family ranking and automatic scanner advisory selection, paired replacement and runtime readiness. No operational run or active model/policy promotion.
grain: One case-sensitive mint mean captured-positive utility, anchored at its earliest original OOS decision; whole fixed UTC hour buckets are resampled together.

findings.evidence: The native later-cohort selector approved 200 synthetic tokens in 50 minutes, with 20 positive labels, perfect scores and capture lift10, as bootstrap_validated_scanner_ranker. Initial native assertion failed in2.74s. This is a software support defect, not an observed trade or financial return.
findings.repair: Retain original OOS decision timestamps through family forward predictions, holdout evaluation and same-cohort challenger/incumbent comparison. Current approval requires token support and two fixed-origin one-hour bucket checks.

method.selection: Original model-fit top-k capacities and exact ties are unchanged. Temporal resampling holds observed cuts fixed.
method.anchor: Each mint mean is anchored at the earliest original OOS decision timestamp, not close time, sample order or scoring-fold label.
method.resampling: 1000 deterministic draws of whole UTC hour buckets at offsets0 and1800seconds. Each draw aggregates bucket delta sums / token counts, retaining token-weighted utility. The conservative lower bound is the minimum of the two fifth-percentile bounds.
method.support: At least30unique tokens,5positive tokens,5buckets and3positive-containing buckets at each origin. Lower bounds and mean gain must be positive. Missing/partial/non-time clocks remain unknown.
method.declaration: Current typed schemes, unique sorted bucket IDs, token/positive-count conservation and utility consistency are required; current combined token/time declarations must belong to the same original utility.
limits: One-hour length and two fixed origins are a prespecified burst-sensitivity diagnostic, not an empirically calibrated dependence horizon or proof of stationary independent epochs.
Each repeated token remains one mean with its earliest anchor. This does not test dependence from later decisions of that mint, between creators, or across longer market regimes.
The bootstrap holds observed selection cuts fixed; it is not fresh full-strategy execution, costed financial acceptance or future coverage.
